title: Prior Authorization Units Ledger: Units Asked For on a Transition-of-Care Request
content:
**Ledger rule.** Under Prior Authorization, the units a transition-of-care request asks for are the units requested on the member's earlier Prairie Ridge approval for the same service code, less the units Prairie Ridge covered on that approval. The units Prairie Ridge covered are the units granted on that approval less the units released from it. The resulting figure is counted in whole units, is never below zero and is never more than the class's most units per approval.

## Terms of the ledger rule

| Quantity | How it is read |
|---|---|
| Units requested on the earlier approval | the request figure recorded on the earlier Prairie Ridge approval, which carried over the units the prior plan's authorization had left |
| Units granted | all grant entries posted on the earlier approval, added together |
| Units released | all release entries posted on the earlier approval, added together, whether released at expiry or on a void |
| Units covered | units granted less units released |
| Units asked for | units requested less units covered, held at no less than zero and no more than the class's most units per approval |

The units covered are worked out first, as one figure; that figure is then taken from the units requested; the floor of zero and the ceiling of the class's most units per approval apply to what remains.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

All inputs below are hypothetical and chosen only to show the arithmetic; the class ceiling used is a hypothetical 12 units.

| Case | Requested | Granted | Released | Covered | Requested less covered | Units asked for |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 20 | 12 | 4 | 8 | 12 | 12 |
| B | 20 | 6 | 0 | 6 | 14 | 12 (ceiling) |
| C | 12 | 12 | 0 | 12 | 0 | 0 |
| D | 12 | 12 | 5 | 7 | 5 | 5 |
| E | 10 | 12 | 0 | 12 | below zero | 0 (floor) |

Cases C and D differ only in the units released from the earlier approval: every unit released lowers the units covered by one and raises the units asked for by one, up to the ceiling.
